hdec-01-c1.text: Faculty of Classics, University of Cambridge (Mycenaean Epigraphy Project). Michael Ventris. University of Cambridge, Faculty of Classics.
hdec-01-c1.quote: He took the opportunity to announce his decipherment and it was broadcast to the world on 1 July 1952.
hdec-01-c1.claim: Once Michael Ventris assigned sound values in 1952, Linear B turned out to be an early form of Greek

hdec-01-c1.text: Šárka Velhartická (2017). The Agreement on the Publication of the Hittite Texts and the Decipherment of the Hittite Language. Historica Olomucensia 53.
hdec-01-c1.quote: He presented his discovery in a lecture in Berlin on 24 November 1915
hdec-01-c1.claim: scholars could sound them out years before Bedřich Hrozný showed in 1915 what language they recorded

hdec-01-c1.text: Claude Rilly (Linguistics Venues Calendar, University of Chicago) (2024). Meroitic Phonology, Syntax, and Linguistic Family. University of Chicago, Voices (Linguistics).
hdec-01-c1.quote: I have shown that Meroitic belonged to a branch of the Nilo-Saharan phylum that I have named Northern East Sudanic (NES).
hdec-01-c1.claim: Claude Rilly has argued that it belongs to the Northern East Sudanic branch of Nilo-Saharan

hdec-01-c3.text: Center for Online Judaic Studies. Ugaritic Alphabet Tablet, 14th-13th century BCE. COJS.
hdec-01-c3.quote: these newly discovered tablets contained fewer than 30 distinct symbols.
hdec-01-c3.claim: When the tablets from Ras Shamra in Syria proved in 1929 to use fewer than 30 signs

hdec-01-c3.text: Swansea University, Ancient World. The Phaistos disc (disk). Swansea University.
hdec-01-c3.quote: a pictographic collection of 45 different signs across the two sides of the disc
hdec-01-c3.claim: The Phaistos Disc shows 45 distinct signs, a syllabary-sized number, but its roughly 240 stamped signs
